speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To narrow this down, have you experienced any recent headache, neck stiffness, or seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of headache and seizures is noted. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, have you noticed any new muscle stiffness, tremors, or difficulty swallowing since starting this medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CPK, Electrolytes, LFTs.
REQUEST IMAGES: None indicated at this stage given the classic clinical presentation.
